title: stream-repair-at-edge-late-segment-reconstruction-and-causal-ordering
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Multiple customer escalations reported intermittent truncated streamed responses (SSE) from the Hosted API where clients receive partial final outputs or duplicate token fragments after a reconnect. This ticket tracks triage, root-cause analysis, developer fixes across the serving runtime and gateway, and the rollout plan to eliminate the class of failures while preserving low tail latency.
reproduction_steps: 1) Tail-heavy prompt that produces ~2k tokens (use customer corpus) against hosted model:v1-large with streaming enabled.
2) During generation, simulate network blips: close TCP connection mid-stream and reconnect within 2-6 seconds.
3) Observe resumed stream: in ~30% of runs client sees repeated fragments or missing tail tokens compared to a non-interrupted generation.
4) Run with KV-cache pressure: trigger background eviction by running concurrent long sequences on same host; failure rate increases.
5) Reproduce with both standard public endpoint and with Dedicated routing to confirm behavior across deployment modes.
root_cause: Race between the new session handoff/opaque session ID mechanism and KV-cache eviction plus gateway resume logic. When a connection is closed mid-stream, the gateway issues a resume request referencing a session checkpoint. If the runtime has evicted relevant KV pages (or compacted an internal buffer) before the resume is reconciled, the resumed stream can replay a cached fragment while the runtime generates a fresh tail — producing duplicates or truncated final tokens. In some cases the resume handshake completed against a different model variant replica that had a slightly divergent tokenization state (minor byte-level mismatch) leading to partial output mismatches.
proposed_fix: 1) Runtime: persist a small immutable tail-snapshot (last 1.5–3k tokens or last 30s of output whichever is smaller) per session until explicit checkpoint-confirmation from gateway; store with checksum and sequence metadata.

2) Gateway: validate resume against tail-snapshot checksum; if mismatch, trigger a full-request replay path or fallback to non-streaming finalization endpoint rather than attempting incremental stitch.
3) KV cache policy: mark resume-protected sessions as eviction-ineligible for a short grace window (configurable, default 60s) to avoid losing resume context under bursty memory pressure.
4) Introduce an idempotent resume token that includes replica generation id + session nonce to fence against resume-to-stale-replicas.
5) Client guidance: backoff and idempotent resume flow with explicit 'finalize' call option; document recommended keepalive/heartbeat intervals and SDK changes.
6) Add server-side deduplication at token-boundary granularity for short overlaps (<= 512 tokens) as a last-resort smoothing mechanism.
7) Put fixes behind a rollout feature flag and enable for customer buckets incrementally.
8) Create a compatibility shim for older SDKs to gracefully degrade to non-resume behavior when session fencing fails.
9) Update model-onboarding checklist to verify tokenization determinism across replicas and quantization profiles.
10) Add regression tests and chaos tests (connection kill, eviction, replica restart) to CI and canary harnesses.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (hotfix): deploy gateway validation and temporary conservative behavior that forces non-resume finalization for impacted customers. Canary 1 host, 1% traffic.
Phase 1: deploy runtime tail-snapshot and idempotent resume token. Canary 5% traffic for 48h measuring duplicate-token-rate, stream-error-rate, and latency p95.
Phase 2: enable KV eviction grace window and replica fencing. Canary 20% for 72h; add automatic rollback trigger on >3x duplicate-token-rate or increased customer complaints.
Phase 3: enable server-side dedupe and SDK guideline rollouts. Gradual ramp to 100% over 2 weeks with post-rollout monitoring.
Phase 4: postmortem and permanent instrumentation retention changes; update SLAs and console messaging where appropriate.
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotent resume token generation and validation
Integration tests: end-to-end SSE resume with induced eviction windows and cross-replica resume attempts
Chaos tests: connection flapping, replica restarts during midstream, rapid memory pressure to trigger KV eviction
Load tests: validate no regression in token throughput or added latency p99 under 4k concurrent streams
Compatibility tests: older SDKs and non-streaming fallbacks
Customer scenario harnesses: replay top 10 failing customer prompts from incident logs
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: resume_checksum_mismatch_rate > 0.5% for 15m => paged to SRE
Alert: duplicate_token_rate spike > 2x baseline and customer complaints > 3 in 1h => SE on-call notification
Dashboard: per-customer stream health with ability to filter by model, region, and replica generation
SLO: ensure resumed_stream_success_rate >= 99.5% after rollout for hosted customers
customer_communications: Initial: Acknowledge issue to impacted customers with incident ID, short description, and recommended short-term workaround (disable resume / use finalize endpoint)
Follow-up: notify when hotfix gateway behavior is in place and ask for validation on their side
Final: post-rollout note with technical summary, what changed, and mitigation steps taken; offer one-on-one session for customers with custom routing (Dedicated/Private)
Support playbook: template response, reproduction steps customers can run, logs we need (session id, request id, timestamps), and expected timing for full fix
notes: On initial triage we prioritized a gateway-side conservative fallback to stop regressions for critical customers while runtime work progressed.
There is a small performance/cost tradeoff: holding immutable tail-snapshots increases memory usage per active session; we will tune via configurable grace window and sampling.
Cross-team coordination required: Serving Runtime, Gateway, SDK, DevEx (docs), SRE, and Customer Success.
Suggested owner rotation for on-call coverage during rollout: Asha (lead), Marco (runtime), Priya (gateway), Jen (SRE).
Goal: eliminate recurrence and ship long-term fix by 2026-03-28; monitor for 30 days after 100% rollout.
